newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand says baht fixing change can wait.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand says baht fixing change can wait.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday a change to the fixing of the baht currency was appropriate but should wait until the Thai money market and volatile interbank rates stabilise.

Rerngchai, asked if the central bank would move to widen a four satangs spread within which it trades baht/dollar with commercial banks, said: "Any change should wait until the situation is calmer...I think it is appropriate but let's wait until it is calmer."
Thai interbank rates have fluctuated sharply in the past month on volatile money market liquidity, partly attributed to local speculation on a bullish U.S. dollar.

The central bank and finance ministry officials have said since the second half of last year that a widened trading range for the baht would help discourage speculation against the currency which periodically came under pressure amid market rumours that it may be devalued to help weak Thai exports.
The officials said a wider baht trading range would also help stem a heavy influx of cheaper short-term foreign funds brought in last year to arbitrage on high Thai interest rates.

Rerngchai declined to say how much the current four satang trading band should be widened but currency dealers have said the range should be at least nine satangs to curb heavy inflow of foreign funds.
